title: Three Months and One Short Page
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：title　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 title 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the writer ① chose the title that no reader in the study would have described, and he said the choosing was the whole of the month. The ② title, meaning the heading itself and not the page, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; a title, he said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ title in that study had the same short page beside it, and the ④ title at the far shelf, meaning the draft they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A title, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the writer said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the title was the whole of the matter, meaning the honour and not the heading. The ⑥ title, meaning the honour and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; title, he said, is either something you choose or the only word that means both a heading and an honour. He said the honour is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ title had become a line in a manuscript, and the manuscript had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ title of the whole thing, the writer wrote in January, was one study and three months of describing; title, he said, is either the draft at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ title I remember is the heading described in the manuscript, which closed in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the study. A ⑩ title, my mother said in 1973, is the only heading that improves by being described; every title, she said, is an honour that has agreed to look like a heading. She said the honour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 标题；头衔（指书斋里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 标题；头衔（指那个标题本身，与薄薄的书页相对）
C. 固定搭配：choose the title 定这一个标题
D. n. 标题；头衔（指留给孩子们誊的那一份）
E. n. 标题之事（抽象总称，指一处书斋的标题之事）
F. n. 标题；头衔（指手稿里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 标题、名分（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 名分（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: chose the title that no reader in the study would have described
The title, meaning the heading itself and not the page
the title at the far shelf
the title was the whole of the matter
the title had become a line in a manuscript
The title of the whole thing
A title, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: choose the title 意为“定这一个标题”，1964 年那位写作者把书斋里没有一位读者肯描述的一个标题做了一遍。
title 意为“标题；头衔”，指那个标题本身而不是薄薄的书页，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
title 意为“标题；头衔”，指书斋里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。
title 意为“标题；头衔”，指最远那层书架的留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
title 意为“标题、名分”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个名分就是那件事的全部。
title 意为“名分”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个标题，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
title 意为“标题；头衔”，指手稿里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1969 年这一个成了手稿里的一行。
title 意为“标题之事”，写作者一月写道，整件事的标题之事是一处书斋和三个月份的描述。
title 意为“标题；头衔”，我记得的是手稿里描述过的那一个，1971 年写就了，至今仍被说成书斋里最安静的一个。
title 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，标题是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的标题。
